messages:
alex: Heads-up — seeing intermittent OOMs + container restarts on nodes that received the CUDA 12 image roll this morning. kubelet shows containers failing with NVRTC/PTX cache errors. :thinking:
infra-bot: image-push:redwood/runtime-cu12:v1.4.2 pushed to eu-west-2 at 08:12 UTC. Canary rollout started to 5 nodes.
alex: repro on two canaries so far — app pods that do JIT compile (custom ops) hit errors like `ptx_cache: failed to compile ptx` and dmesg has `nvidia: kernel module version magic mismatch` lines.
maria: can you paste the exact dmesg? and which driver version is on the host?
alex: dmesg snippet: `nvidia: module license 'NVIDIA' taints kernel; nvidia: version magic 5.15.0-101-generic SMP mod_unload ` vs host driver built for 5.19`; `NVRTC ERROR: PTX compilation failed: incompatible libdevice`
sam: this smells like a host-driver vs toolkit ABI mismatch, or the toolkit binary bundles were built with a different gcc/abi. CUDA 12 changed a few ABI things w/ libdevice and nvrtc. Also seen NVRTC failures when ptx cache is stale across container restarts.
lee: quick triage steps: `nvidia-smi -a` on offending node, `modinfo nvidia | grep vermagic`, and check container runtime `ldd` on libnvrtc.so inside image. If vermagic differs, kernel module reload or driver upgrade/downgrade is needed.
alex: nvidia-smi shows DriverVersion=535.54, toolkit image uses cudatoolkit 12.1. Host kernel is 5.15.0-101. `modinfo nvidia | grep vermagic` shows `5.19.0-47` in module build info (so module mismatches kernel).
maria: oh — hosts were partially patched earlier this week (kernel roll) but we didn't rebuild kernel-modules on the fleet. That would cause the module/verm mismatch. Why did the canary land on those hosts? scheduler affinity picked them.
oncall-bot: alert: node/node-iu7k in eu-west-2 marked NotReady due to kubelet crashloop (since 09:03).
sam: two fallout paths: 1) revert runtime image to previous CUDA 11.x variant to stop new PTX paths (fast but loses CUDA12 features), 2) fix host kernel/module by rebuilding and rolling kernel modules or remediating hosts (slower).
lee: we should also consider a container-level workaround: set `CUDA_CACHE_DISABLE=1` to avoid reusing ptX cache (temp mitigation) and restart affected pods. It avoids PTX cache reuse but is not a fix.
alex: putting node taint + cordon on the 5 problematic hosts now. Will kick ongoing rebuilds off those hosts. :hammer:
maria: also start a rebuild queue for images that were built on gcc13 vs runtime host gcc mismatch. I counted ~120 images in our private registry that tag as `built-with-gcc=13`. Prioritize TF-serving, embeddings, and customer-facing endpoints.
sam: costing note — if we overcordon eu-west-2 and shift load to us-west-2, we'll hit spot/core shortage and temporary burst infra cost. We should coordinate with capacity planning before broad tainting.
lee: created INFRA-652 to track the rebuild/backlog and node remediation. Assigned to infra-image-team and infra-ops. Link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INFRA-652
oncall-bot: deploy-bot: rolling-restart request queued for 18 pods flagged critical.
alex: plan: 1) revert the runtime tag for the main hosted fleet to `runtime-cu11-stable` (rollback) — immediate. 2) cordon+taint affected hosts, drain non-critical pods. 3) push `CUDA_CACHE_DISABLE=1` env on canaries and critical services as hotfix. 4) schedule kernel-module rebuild + driver install for the host kernel mismatch during off-peak window (eu-west-2 night). 5) run prioritized image rebuilds (INFRA-652) to produce cudatoolkit12-safe images.
maria: I'm running a quick canary rebuild for our TF-serving image with `gcc 11` build flags and will push a test tag in ~30m. Will report results. :eyes:
lee: FYI - add a prometheus alert for `nvrtc_errors_total > 0` and `nvidia_module_vermagic_mismatch` so we catch next time before user impact.
sam: agree. Also add a rollout policy: when switching major toolkits require host-driver parity gates in the cluster-state checklist.
alex: ok I'm starting the rollback now. Will update thread.
maria: can anyone pick up customer comms? CS already pinged about 3 cases. I'll draft a status blurb.
oncall-bot: status update: rollback initiated at 09:20 UTC, expected ~15m to propagate to hosted API nodes.
